title: hash joins on shop: which side gets hashed, and a build side that stops fitting in memory

steps.sql: SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE id IN (1, 12, 47, 92, 511, 529, 566, 1596) ORDER BY id
steps.note: eight orders: the probe side of the small join.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE id <= 5 ORDER BY id

EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id
steps.note: orders first in FROM: postgres hashes customers, the smaller side, and streams orders past it.

data: ->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on customers c (actual rows=2000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.id, c.name FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
steps.note: customers first in FROM: the same plan. the order you write the tables in doesn't pick the build side.

data: ->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on customers c (actual rows=2000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.customer_id, o.status, o.ordered_at, o.shipped_at, oi.product_id, oi.qty
FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON o.id = oi.order_id
steps.note: the default work_mem, 4MB, times hash_mem_multiplier 2: all 10,000 orders fit in one hash table.

data: ->  Seq Scan on order_items oi (actual rows=24942.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
SET work_mem = '256kB';
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.customer_id, o.status, o.ordered_at, o.shipped_at, oi.product_id, oi.qty
FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON o.id = oi.order_id
steps.note: 256kB, so 512kB for the hash table: postgres splits both sides into 2 batches and keeps one in memory.

data: Buffers: shared hit=242, temp read=82 written=82
->  Seq Scan on order_items oi (actual rows=24942.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
SET work_mem = '128kB';
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT o.customer_id, o.status, o.ordered_at, o.shipped_at, oi.product_id, oi.qty
FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON o.id = oi.order_id
steps.note: 128kB: 4 batches. three quarters of both sides go to temp files and come back later.

data: Buffers: shared hit=242, temp read=128 written=128
->  Seq Scan on order_items oi (actual rows=24942.00 loops=1)
->  Seq Scan on orders o (actual rows=10000.00 loops=1)
